Class LessonsLearned

java.lang.Object
entityClasses.LessonsLearned
public class LessonsLearned extends Object

Title: LessonsLearned Class

Description: This LessonsLearned class represents one lesson learned in the system. It holds the same lesson information our Database class and the Role1 (contributor) and Role2 (curator) home pages already use: the contributor who added it, its title and description, the locks a curator can set, the curator's notes, and the experience entries added to it. It also checks that each value is valid before it is saved. The database work for each Create, Read, Update, and Delete (CRUD) operation is done by the LessonsLearnedList class, which stores lessons in the lessonsDB table and experience entries in the experienceDB table.

The user stories in "Lessons Learned System - Initial User Stories V1" are not numbered, so we gave them the short names below. These names are used in the comments of this class, LessonsLearnedList, and the tests so you can see which code satisfies which requirement.

  • C-1: A contributor adds a lesson with core information and can see and manage it. Other roles may update, delete, or lock fields of it, and the contributor can't see or change what those roles add.
  • C-2: A contributor sees a list of their lessons, picks one to look at, and sees which fields are locked. A locked lesson, or one with a locked field, can't be deleted.
  • C-3: A contributor adds experience information to a lesson: what was done, how it was done, how long it took, and the effort used by the team members.
  • C-4: A contributor only sees their own content, including after a curator edits it, and never sees other contributors' lessons.
  • EC-1: (Phase Three epic) AI writing, brainstorming, and search tools that help a contributor write a lesson.
  • V-1, V-2, V-3: (Phase Three) viewers list all lessons, search by keyword, and open one lesson.
  • CU-1 to CU-5: (Phase Three curator epics) AI search terms, AI editing help, merged time and effort statistics, showing or hiding those statistics, and locking.
  • TC: our TP2 Test Cases document (TC-1 to TC-24).
  • AIC: our AICoaching.pdf, which lists Title (priority 1) and Description (priority 2) as the input fields to coach.
  • DB: the lessonsDB and experienceDB tables and lesson methods already in our Database class, which the Role1 and Role2 home pages use.

How this class supports the Contributor User Stories:

  • C-1: the title, description, and category attributes hold the core information, create() saves it, and validate() makes sure only valid values are saved. The lock attributes and curatorNotes let curators work on the lesson, and contributorView() hides what they add.
  • C-2: the contributor attribute links each lesson to its owner, isFieldLocked() tells the GUI which fields to make read only, and isDeletable() stops locked lessons from being deleted.
  • C-3: the Experience class inside this class holds one experience entry, and addExperience() saves it.
  • C-4: contributorView() removes the curator-only information, and lastEditedBy shows the contributor that a curator changed their lesson.

How this class is ready for AI coaching (EC-1, AIC): the check methods are public and static, so a coaching tool can call checkTitle() and checkDescription() on text while the contributor is still typing, before anything is saved. AICoaching.pdf plans LanguageTool for the title and Grammarly for the description; their suggestions only change the text the contributor enters, so no new attributes are needed for them. The same checks still run in validate() when the lesson is saved, so coaching can never let invalid input through.

CRUD operations: Create is create() and addExperience(); Read is read() and the getters; Update is update() and the setters; Delete is delete(). Each one passes the database work to LessonsLearnedList.

Like the PasswordEvaluator and UserNameRecognizer classes, each check method returns an empty String when the value is valid, or an error message the GUI can show.
